cards.text: Why does a 12 V car bulb burn out instantly on 230 V mains? One simple formula explains it.

cards.title: The three players
cards.text: Voltage (V) is the push. Current (I, in amps) is the flow. Resistance (R, in ohms) is how hard the path resists the flow. More push means more flow; more resistance means less.

cards.title: The formula
cards.text: V = I × R. Cover the one you want: I = V / R, R = V / I. That's Ohm's law, and you will use it constantly.

cards.question: A 12 V battery is connected to a 6 Ω resistor. What current flows?

cards.text: Find any power adapter at home and read its label. Note the output voltage and current.
Connect an LED straight to a 9 V battery and it dies in a flash. A 30-cent resistor saves it.

cards.title: Drop the extra voltage
cards.text: A red LED needs about 2 V and 20 mA. The resistor must 'eat' the rest: 9 V − 2 V = 7 V. R = 7 V / 0.02 A = 350 Ω. Use the next standard value up: 390 Ω.
On a 5 V USB supply: (5 − 2) / 0.02 = 150 Ω. A 220 Ω resistor works fine and is slightly dimmer and safer.

cards.question: Why choose 390 Ω instead of exactly 350 Ω?
choices: It's the next standard value up, keeping current safely below the limit
350 Ω would give too little current
cards.explanation: Rounding up to a standard value keeps the current slightly lower, which protects the LED.
